structured.answer: After 8 years, putting in 500 ₪ a month, the calculator says about 68,853 ₪ would be left for me (I'd have put in 48,000). For 4 years it gives no number at all. It says "לעצמאים עוד אין כאן חישוב למשיכה לפני 6 שנים", only that I'd pay tax, so I'll ask you or the bank about that part.

stuck.where: Calculator result at year 4 and year 5
stuck.why: The only number shown (25,725 / 32,755) sits above an empty dashed box. Its label was hidden behind the round up-arrow button, so I thought it might be my fund's amount. After scrolling I saw it was 'אותו כסף בחשבון ניירות ערך', something else.
It's a slider. I don't use those, so I pressed the year numbers under the bars instead. That worked, but it wasn't obvious it would.
The page says self-employed people get the exemption up to 20,566 ₪ a year, but the box asks for a monthly amount (500). I didn't want to work out the division, so I left 500.

findings.what: For self-employed people the calculator shows nothing before year 6, only an empty dashed box. The one number shown there belongs to a different thing (a securities account), so it's easy to mistake for my own result.
The round 'back to top' arrow covers the label under the comparison bar ('אותו כסף בחשבון ניירות ערך').
The example the calculator uses is a share track ('מיטב השתלמות עוקב מדד S&P500'), and that's only said further down. Someone who wants safe money isn't told that the 7% assumes shares.
The year is chosen with a slider. Pressing the year numbers works, but nothing says so plainly.
The annual limit for self-employed is given per year (20,566 ₪), but the box asks for a monthly amount.
Dark background with grey text, and some of the smaller grey lines are hard to read.
findings.where: Whole page, e.g. 'גררו את הסמן...' hint
